ops.title: rm→trash rewrite lacks root/home guards (review finding on ae212caf)
ops.body:
An adversarial review pass (gpt-5.6-sol, 2026-07-18, run alongside the 9.30.0 tables wave) rated this a **blocker** in the 9.29.0 rm→trash commit `ae212caf`, which is not this wave's code — recorded here for the owner to adjudicate.

**Finding**: broad destructive targets are auto-rewritten to `trash` with no filesystem-root, home, or workspace-parent guard. Probes returned allow-rewrites for:

- `rm -rf --no-preserve-root /` → `/opt/fake/trash /`
- `rm -rf /Users/yasyf/Code` → `/usr/bin/trash /Users/yasyf/Code`

Both were **denied** before `ae212caf`. Trash is recoverable by design, but moving `~/Code` (every repo) or attempting `/` to the Trash is arguably still deny-tier. The commit's own carve-outs (repo-root deletes, oversized/unverifiable globs, non-macOS) stay denied; the gap is only the very-large-blast-radius *outside-repo literal* targets.

**Suggested fix shape**: keep the trash rewrite, but deny when the resolved target is `/`, a user home, or an ancestor of the current repo root (the threat model in cc-notes doc 54548bc9 already names these tiers). Evidence with exact probe commands: finder report preserved in the 9.30.0 wave records.
